name: Ivy Burke
life: “I still remember saving two places at a crowded supper table.” People around the downtown fountain know Ivy by a small Saturday habit. Ivy keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I want to stay their carer. Our spare room pays the mortgage with a lodger in it.
appearance: Ivy is easy to recognize by a high puff tied with plain cord and a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Usually dressed in a faded indigo overshirt with a replacement button a shade darker than the others, Ivy starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak when listening.
personality: Ivy treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To keep both foster placements financially possible.
family: Ken Calloway is Ivy’s cousin raised in the same household. Ivy chooses whether to use it. Ken saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *Closing soup*, Ken says, “I was ashamed my family lived on leftovers.”
connections: Patrick Osborne. The carer and the lodger negotiate two families' housing at once. Other connections include Cyrus Keller (foster child), Dale Lane (foster child).

reactions.situation: A caseworker asks the foster siblings to describe sharing
reactions.response: Ivy gives each sibling room to describe sharing separately.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Ivy asks which apartment is expecting someone home and makes sure that household knows about the delay.

reactions.situation: If a frightened person needs longer
reactions.response: Ivy changes the plan openly and takes responsibility for the delay.
